intro.title: Write retry with exponential backoff
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a function that retries a failing operation using exponential backoff, a common technique for handling temporary network or service errors. You'll learn to implement a retry mechanism that waits progressively longer between attempts, such as doubling the wait time after each failure. The core programming concepts involve using async/await for asynchronous operations, setTimeout for delays, and a loop with conditional logic to control retries. You'll work with JavaScript promises, error handling with try/catch, and basic arithmetic to calculate backoff intervals. By the end, you'll have a reusable utility that makes your applications more resilient to transient failures.
intro.usecase: In real-world applications, network requests often fail due to temporary issues like server overload or spotty connections. Exponential backoff with retry is a critical pattern for handling these failures gracefully, preventing your app from overwhelming the server with repeated immediate attempts. You'll see this in user-facing features like payment processing forms, where a transaction might need a few retries to succeed, or in data dashboards that automatically refresh critical metrics after a network hiccup. Implementing this pattern ensures your application is resilient and provides a smooth, reliable experience even under unstable conditions.
